title: Equivariant geometric-normal preparation by a finite inseparable constant extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $S$ an integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme. Let $J$ be a finite group acting on $k$ by field automorphisms and on $S$ by compatible scheme automorphisms, with no faithfulness requirement. There is a finite purely inseparable extension $l/k$ with a $J$-action extending the given action on $k$, such that the reduced scheme $T=(S\times_k\operatorname{Spec}l)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is integral and its normalization $n:B\to S_l$ is finite and surjective. The scheme $B$ is normal integral, projective and proper of finite type over $l$, and geometrically normal over $l$. There is a compatible $J$-action on $B$ for which $n$ and $q:B\to S_l\to S$ are equivariant. The field inclusions $k(S)\hookrightarrow k(B)$ and $l\hookrightarrow k(B)$ commute with the $J$-actions. Every subgroup of $J$ acting trivially on $k$ acts trivially on $l$. In characteristic zero one can take $l=k$.

Here $S_l=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}l$, and $n$ is the normalization of $T$ followed by its closed immersion in $S_l$. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Geometrically normal means that this holds after every field extension of $l$. Schemes, fields, integrality, projectivity, finite type, properness, finite morphisms, surjectivity, base change, reduction, normalization, function fields and purely inseparable extensions use [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-pc-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], [def-sc-normalization], [def-sc-function-field] and [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-geonormal-insep] to $S$ to obtain a finite purely inseparable extension $e/k$ whose reduced-base-change normalization $N_e$ is geometrically normal over $e$. Choose a perfect purely inseparable overfield $P/k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-purely-inseparable-overfield]. In positive characteristic write $p=\operatorname{char}k$. There is a unique $k$-embedding $e\hookrightarrow P$: send $x\in e$ with $x^{p^r}=a\in k$ to the unique $p^r$-th root of $a$ in $P$. Existence follows from perfection; uniqueness from injectivity of Frobenius. Using a common exponent proves compatibility with addition, multiplication and every relation among the elements of $e$. Thus regard $e$ as a subfield of $P$. In characteristic zero pure inseparability gives $e=P=k$.

source.place: Tag 0BXT, lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal; algebra.tex Tag 046W, lemma-perfection; root embedding written out

proof.text: Extend the given field automorphism $\sigma_j$ of $k$ to $P$ by $\widetilde\sigma_j(x)^{p^r}=\sigma_j(x^{p^r})$ whenever $x^{p^r}\in k$. The unique root exists because $P$ is perfect. Increasing $r$ does not change the root, and raising to a common $p$-power proves additivity, multiplicativity and $\widetilde\sigma_i\widetilde\sigma_j=\widetilde\sigma_{ij}$; $\widetilde\sigma_{j^{-1}}$ is the inverse. Let $l$ be the subfield of $P$ generated by all $\widetilde\sigma_j(e)$, $j\in J$. Each image is finite over $k$, and the orbit has finitely many members, so choosing finite generating sets for these images shows $l/k$ is finite. Every element of $l\subset P$ has a $p$-power in $k$, so $l/k$ and $l/e$ are purely inseparable. The group permutes these image fields, hence preserves $l$. If $j$ fixes $k$, the displayed root equation gives $\widetilde\sigma_j(x)=x$ for all $x\in P$. Thus any subgroup fixing $k$ fixes $l$ pointwise. In characteristic zero use the original action and $l=k$.

source.place: Tag 046W, lemma-perfection, explicit unique-root and finite-orbit argument of the worker

proof.text: Put $S_l=S\times_k\operatorname{Spec}l$ and $T=(S_l)_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], $|S_l|\to|S|$ is a homeomorphism. Reduction is the identity on the underlying space by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], so $T$ is irreducible and nonempty; being reduced, it is integral. Projectivity of $S_l/l$ follows from [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-projective-components] to $S_l$: its normalization is the normalization $B$ of $T$, its map $n:B\to S_l$ is finite and surjective, and $B$ is projective and proper over $l$. Since $S_l$ has one irreducible component, the decomposition in that node has one member, giving normality and integrality of $B$. Properness includes finite type. Apply [lem-trf-normalization-inseparable-base-change] with $C=S$, $k_1=e$, $k_2=l$ and the geometrically normal $N_e$ from step 1. It identifies $B$ with $N_e\times_e l$ over $S_l$ and asserts that $B$ is geometrically normal over $l$. The statement allows $e=k$ and $l=e$.

The actions on $S$ and $l$ induce an action on $S_l$ by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-base-change]; on the field factor use $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma_j^{-1})$, so that scheme actions compose in the given group order. They preserve the nilradical, hence induce automorphisms $h_j$ of $T$ and make $T	o S_l	o S$ equivariant [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Let $
u:B	o T$ be normalization. Each $h_j
u$ is dominant and has normal integral source, so [lem-sbc-normalization-dominant-lift] supplies a unique dominant $a_j:B	o B$ with $
u a_j=h_j
u$. Both $a_i a_j$ and $a_{ij}$ factor $h_{ij}
u$, so uniqueness identifies them; the identity lift is the identity, and inverse indices give inverses. Thus these lifts form an action. Composing with $T	o S_l$ proves equivariance of $n$; composing with $S_l	o S$ proves equivariance of $q$. Composing further with the structural maps proves compatibility with the action on $l$ and its restriction to $k$.

source.place: Tag 035Q, lemma-normalization-normal (4); action laws by uniqueness; fibre-product and reduction definitions

proof.text: Finally $q$ is dominant: $n$ is surjective and $S_l\to S$ is a homeomorphism by step 3. It therefore maps the generic point of $B$ to that of $S$. Pullback on their generic stalks gives a unital homomorphism of fields $k(S)\to k(B)$, which is injective [def-sc-function-field]. The structure map similarly gives an injective homomorphism $l\to k(B)$, since $B$ is nonempty and integral. For the actions on function fields take inverse pullback, $j\cdot f=(a_{j^{-1}})^*f$, and likewise on $S$. The two equivariance identities of step 4, restricted to generic stalks and pulled back, state exactly that these two field embeddings commute with the $J$-actions. Step 2 already gives the kernel assertion and the choice $l=k$ in characteristic zero.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O4-335eb46bd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all ten cited nodes in full, plus Stacks varieties 0BXT, 0C3N and 0GK4. This is a first split: the base proof was empty, the statement is unchanged apart from doubled TeX backslashes, and there are no new nodes. Step 1: geonormal-insep gives e; the perfect overfield P is a Mathlib leaf; the unique-root embedding e→P is correct. Step 2: I checked that σ̃_j is a well-defined automorphism of P and that the σ̃_j form a group action. The orbit compositum l is finite, purely inseparable and J-stable, and a subgroup fixing k fixes l pointwise. In characteristic 0, l=k. Step 3: the homeomorphism lemma plus reduction make T integral, and S_l is projective. projective-components gives B finite surjective, projective, proper, normal and integral, with one component. trf-normalization-inseparable-base-change with C=S, k1=e, k2=l gives B ≅ N_e×_e l, geometrically normal. Step 4: dominant-lift uniqueness gives the group laws for the a_j, and equivariance of n, q and the structure map follows. Step 5: the generic point maps to the generic point, and with inverse pullback both field embeddings are equivariant. I tested trivial and nonfaithful actions, characteristic 0, dimension 0 and nonreduced S_l. The duplicate search found no equivariant duplicate. I accept the six declared generic tool_uses. On the batch-5 flag: lem-trf-normalization-inseparable-base-change is pure scheme theory. Its 675-node closure contains only two other trf nodes, both commutative algebra, and no trace-formula, Poincaré or nt-assume content, so it is outside both assumptions. One advisory point: identifying step 1's componentwise normalization with the normalization of (S_e)_red is left implicit, by the same homeomorphism lemma. No SGA is cited. No fixes.
